newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales tumble for second month in a row.
newsitem.headline: French car sales tumble for second month in a row.

text.p: New car sales in France slid 24.6 percent last month after tumbling 33.6 percent in January, the French carmakers association CCFA said on Monday.
It said the two-month drop reflected the market's weakness since the conclusion at the end of September of a state rebate programme that had underpinned demand.
On a comparable day basis -- there were 20 working days last month and 21 in February 1996 -- sales fell 20.9 percent.
Car sales totalled 133,680 units, compared with 177,378 in February 1996 when the new-cars-for-old rebates were on offer.

"As in January, the French car market remained in February at the very low levels observed since the end of the rebate programme and close to the worst sales results recorded in 1993," the CCFA said in a statement.

In contrast with previous months, foreign carmakers fared about as badly as the French. Sales of foreign brands fell 24.1 percent, while sales of French cars dropped 25 percent, leaving them with a 58 percent share of the domestic market.
Car sales by the PSA Peugeot Citroen group fell 29.4 percent last month to 39,716 units, and Renault SA sales fell 19.7 percent to 37,748.

Despite Renault's financial woes -- it expects a huge loss for 1996 and said last week that it would close a plant in Belgium -- its sales performance has been helped by the popularity of the Megane Scenic, a car designed with the proportions of a minivan.
GM Opel sales fell 11.6 percent, Ford car sales fell 26.8 percent, Fiat car sales plunged 44.9 percent, and Volkswagen sales dropped 15 percent in February.
Sales of Japanese cars fell 22 percent, while upmarket manufacturers Mercedes Benz and Volvo recorded sales gains of 3.2 percent and 33.2 percent, respectively.
In the first two months of 1997, 256,000 new cars were sold in France, down 29.3 percent from 361,919 sales in the corresponding 1996 period.
